lines.trans: See you soon!

words.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian for 12. From eleven up, the counted noun stays singular: اتنعش فنجان 'twelve cups'.

examples.trans: We have twelve guests tonight.
It's twelve noon.

meanings.note: Often placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'spare' (مفتاح احتياط a spare key).

examples.trans: I have a spare key in the drawer.
We bought a spare valve for winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Name of the fifth day of the traditional Arabic week ('Thursday', related to خمسة 'five').

examples.text: السوق الشعبي بيفتح يوم الخميس بعد الظهر.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood market opens on Thursday afternoon.

examples.text: رح نستلم الطاولات يوم الخميس الجاي.
examples.trans: We will receive the tables next Thursday.

meanings.note: Saturday (يوم السبت or simply السبت), start of the Jordanian working/market weekend.

examples.text: كل سبت الصبح بنمشي عسوق الحارة.
examples.trans: Every Saturday morning we walk to the neighbourhood market.

examples.text: الخبز الطازة بيجهز يوم السبت الساعة تمانية.
examples.trans: Fresh bread is ready on Saturday at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Form III verb from ب-ر-ك; باركلي means 'congratulate me!' (related to مبروك 'congratulations!').

examples.trans: Congratulate me—I found the lost key in the drawer!

examples.text: كل الجيران إجوا يباركوا لنور عالشغل الجديد.
examples.trans: All the neighbours came to congratulate Nour on the new job.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Preposition 'without'; followed by ما + verb it means 'without -ing' (بدون ما ياخد 'without taking').

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'two' (إنتو التنين 'the two of you'); note homograph التنين ('Monday').

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتوتر, بيتوتر).

examples.trans: When I get nervous, my sentences turn long!

examples.text: لا تتوتر، كل شي رح يمشي تمام.
examples.trans: Do not get nervous, everything will go fine.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of وصّل ('to deliver, drop off; connect wires'); سيارة توصيل means 'delivery van'.

examples.trans: The delivery van pulled up in front of the gate.

examples.text: التوصيل للبيت مجاني إذا طلبنا دزينة.
examples.trans: Home delivery is free if we order a dozen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a garden or yard; a small one is a جنينة, the formal word is حديقة.

examples.trans: We have a small garden behind the house.
The children are playing in the garden.

meanings.note: Active participle of حط ('to put, place').

examples.trans: Mazen has put old boxes on the stairs.
What have you packed inside this suitcase?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبي, بيخبي).

examples.trans: Why did you save it away for me all these years?
She tucked the recipe away in the kitchen notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دوائر.

examples.trans: A paper arrived from the property department.
The department office is downtown.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine market word (from Italian dozzina) for a set of twelve; dual دزينتين ('two dozen' = 24).

examples.trans: We bought a dozen white cups for the café.

examples.text: الدكان بيعمل خصم إذا أخدت دزينتين.
examples.trans: The shop gives a discount if you take two dozen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دكاكين.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I bought milk and bread from the shop.

meanings.note: Feminine noun used in Jordanian weather expressions: الدنيا بتمطر ('it is raining'), الدنيا برد ('it is cold out').

examples.trans: It is raining outside right now.
It is sunny and lovely out this morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: The imperative روق (rawwiq, to a man) or روقي (to a woman) means 'chill, relax'. Related to رايق, calm and in a good mood.

examples.text: روقي يا بنت، لسا في وقت.
examples.trans: Relax, girl, there is still time.
I drink my coffee and relax a bit.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسعار.

examples.trans: Tonight the room is at half price.
The shop's prices are fair and reasonable.

meanings.note: Means 'peace', and in يا سلام! expresses delight ('oh wow! / wonderful!').

examples.text: يا سلام عالشمس الدافية بعد المطر!
examples.trans: Oh how lovely, warm sun after the rain!
They live in safety and peace in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سيارات.

examples.trans: We heard a car stop outside.

examples.text: ما في صوت سيارات جوا الساحة.
examples.trans: There is no sound of cars inside the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian spoken word (from French chauffeur) for a van, taxi, or truck driver.

examples.text: الشوفير وقف سيارة التوصيل قدام البوابة.
examples.trans: The driver parked the delivery van in front of the gate.

examples.text: اتصل الشوفير يسأل عن رقم البيت.
examples.trans: The driver called to ask for the house number.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ضيقة, plural: ضيقين).

examples.trans: The attic stairs are a bit narrow.
Do not enter the narrow alley.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلب, بيطلب).

examples.trans: The postman just asked for my signature.

examples.text: طلبت منه يقابلك هون يوم الجمعة؟
examples.trans: Did you ask him to meet you here on Friday?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طوارئ.

examples.trans: We have a small emergency in the kitchen!
The emergency key hangs beside the door.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطوي, بيطوي).

examples.trans: Fold this sheet and put it in your pocket.
She folded the clean towels in the closet.

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Means both a stone/wooden architectural pillar and a vertical column in a ledger or timetable.

examples.text: قرا مازن العمود التاني بالدفتر بدون نظارة.
examples.trans: Mazen read the second column in the notebook without glasses.

examples.text: علقنا الفانوس جنب عمود الحجر بالساحة.
examples.trans: We hung the lantern beside the stone pillar in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Used as noun in بالغلط ('by mistake') and عالغلط ('for the mistake'), and invariable predicate 'wrong' (في شي غلط something is wrong).

examples.trans: He took the other suitcase by mistake.
Sorry for the mistake, my apologies.

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقول, بيقول).

examples.trans: What does clause fourteen say?
He said thank you and hung up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كراسي.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلاقي, بيلاقي).

examples.trans: Tell me how to find the hardware shop.

examples.text: لقيت هاد الصندوق الخشب ورا الحيط!
examples.trans: I found this wooden box behind the wall!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'why?'.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مكتوبة, plural: مكتوبين).

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'who?' (لمين 'whose? / for whom?').

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of نصف ('half'); used for half hours (السبعة ونص seven thirty) and quantities (نص كاسة half a glass).

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'where?'.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
